scenario_name: Damnoen Saduak van transfer suspended (driver strike)

trigger.reason: Inter-provincial van and minibus drivers strike over fuel-surcharge disputes, suspending all shared van transfers on the Bangkok-Damnoen Saduak route for the day

steps.name: Bangkok to Damnoen Saduak Floating Market

original_plan_for_window.quality_note: Shared van transfer is the only affordable way to reach Damnoen Saduak; the strike leaves no transfer option today, and a private charter would cost several times more

recovery_plans.label: Reorder: old-city temples this morning, market rescheduled
recovery_plans.description: Stay in the city instead of chasing a rural transfer that isn't running. Do a Chinatown food walk plus Wat Arun and Wat Pho, all close together with no long transfer needed. Damnoen Saduak is rescheduled to a later day once the strike resolves.
recovery_plans.tradeoff: Saves 1700 baht and finishes 2 hours earlier since these old-city sites sit a short hop from each other with no long transfer; the floating market moves to a later day once driver transport normalizes.
recovery_plans.best_for: Travelers who want to stay flexible and reattempt the floating market once transport resumes

recovery_plans.label: Substitute: skip the floating market, do in-city heritage instead
recovery_plans.description: Drop the rural day trip entirely. Visit the Jim Thompson House and Erawan Shrine, both fully in-city and unaffected by the strike.
recovery_plans.tradeoff: Saves 1800 baht and about 4.5 hours; trades the floating market for a silk-heritage house museum and a quick shrine visit, both unaffected by the strike.
recovery_plans.best_for: Budget-conscious travelers or those short on time who'd rather not chase a rural day trip

recovery_plans.label: Pivot: relaxed midday, river dinner cruise in the evening
recovery_plans.description: Free up the whole morning. Grab a light lunch of Chinatown street food, then close the day with a scenic Chao Phraya dinner cruise instead of an early rural start.

baseline_for_comparison.note: Compare against original window (2000) plus a separate dinner you'd have paid anyway (~400 at Krua Apsorn)

recovery_plans.tradeoff: Costs 900 less than the original floating-market day plus a normal dinner would have; swaps an early rural start for relaxed street food and a scenic evening river cruise with dinner folded in.
recovery_plans.best_for: Travelers who'd rather sleep in and end the day with a memorable river cruise than chase a rescheduled market trip
